newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps - Fuel oil soft in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps - Fuel oil soft in quiet trade.

text.p: Singapore fuel oil swaps were steady late afternoon on Tuesday in quiet trading but down from Monday on improved supplies in Singapore and fresh offers from Japan and South Korea, traders said.
"The market is not that bullish as there are cargoes coming in from the AG (MidEast) and Venezuela," one trader said.
March fuel oil swaps were last quoted at $102.75/$104.00 per tonne, down from Monday's $104.00/$104.50. It traded at $104.50 per tonne on Monday.
Traders said one 80,000-tonne cargo each from the MidEast and Venezuela is due in Singapore in February.
The softer market they said was also due to the absence of new buying from China and offers for late February and early March lifting cargoes from Japan and South Korea.
Traders said Japan is offering 20,000-40,000 tonnes at $103.00 per tonne on a free-on-board basis Japan, down 50 cents from Monday's offered level.
Gas oil swaps were steady in quiet trading with some players away for the International Petroleum meeting in London.
March swaps were last quoted in Singapore on Tuesday at $25.90/$26.00 per barrel, down from Monday's $26.00/$26.10.
Brokers said the market traded earlier in the day at $25.95 per barrel. The March/April time spread was quoted at 10-20 plus cents, they said.

The jet fuel market firmed slightly in correction to last week's plunge when the market lost around $3.00 per barrel. March regrade or jet fuel/gas oil spread was last quoted at $2.60/$2.85 per barrel, up from Monday's $2.40 bid.
